content.thinking:
I'm planning the file structure, deciding to use the builder API to create a scene and return its root object as the default export.

Now I'm sketching the dwarf's proportions and layout: squat 1.25m build with boxy boots, rod legs, a barrel torso with belt and buckle, broad shoulders with pauldrons, and a helmeted head featuring a bulbous nose, bushy brows, and a braided beard, all positioned with specific coordinates and primitive shapes.

Working out the beard braids as chains of tapering spheres hanging from the chin, tied off with gold rings, plus curling mustache capsules. Then I'm positioning the arms so the dwarf holds a blunderbuss diagonally across his body, stock near the right shoulder and barrel angled forward.

For the gun itself, I'm computing positions along the axis from butt to muzzle to build the stock, lock, barrel, and flared brass muzzle as tapering rod segments with increasing radius toward the bell mouth.

Now I'm positioning the hands as fists gripping the stock and barrel at specific points along that axis, then working out shoulder-to-elbow-to-hand arm geometry for both right and left arms based on those grip points.

I'm checking whether the gun's position intersects with the torso and beard — raising and adjusting the gun's placement near the chest and chin to avoid clipping through the body or facial hair.

Checking the gun's clearance past the beard as it moves forward, then working out the arm geometry—shoulder position, hand placement, and distance to verify the arm length and elbow bend make sense for the pose.

Still defining gun geometry...

Now I'm moving to the figure's lower body: boots with darker soles and toe caps, rolled cuffs, legs as tapered rods connecting hip to ankle, knee pad armor spheres, and a pelvis capsule, before starting on the torso as a barrel shape.

For the torso, I'm abandoning the loft approach since orientation is uncertain and instead using scaled sphere geometries—one for the chest and one for the hips—to approximate the barrel form safely.

Head center sits around y=1.12 with roughly 0.14 radius, bringing total height to about 1.35, which fits a dwarf's proportions fine.

Now I'm thinking through tunic coloring—considering a paint function that creates a tabard-style front pattern mixing gold and blue, with mottling for cloth texture variation.

For skin and beard I'm layering a mottled tan tone for the face, then a grainy orange-red mottle for the beard texture, with the beard built from capsule and sphere shapes chained together.

Now I'm defining the signature braids: two hanging braids at opposite sides of the chin, built from a chain of spheres that shrink in radius as they descend, alternating darker orange grain coloring between segments, with tie bands marking plait divisions.

For the ends, I'm adding gold tassel tips using flattened spheres, and shaping the moustache with capsule sweeps curving outward from the upper lip. I'm placing a small pink-skinned nose sphere and white eye spheres to round out the face.

Still working out face placement...

Now I'm adding helmet details like the nose guard, side horns, crest, and rivets, then shaping the pauldrons as tilted hemisphere forms at the shoulders.

For the bandolier strap, I'm working out how to position it across the chest so it sits on the torso's curved surface rather than sinking inside it—adjusting the sweep points' depth to match the ellipsoid's silhouette at each height.

Then for the shot pouches, I'm thinking of adding small brass cartridge cylinders spaced along the strap, interpolating their positions along the polyline so they orient naturally upward.

Now I'm sizing the belt: a leather cylinder with grain texture around the torso, matching the ellipsoid radii at hip height so it wraps cleanly around the wide and narrow axes of the body.

I'm adding a gold buckle box with a darker inset detail at the center front, plus side pouches positioned just outside the hip radius, and a powder horn accessory hanging from the left side of the belt.

Now I'm defining the arm geometry symmetrically for left and right sides, with upper arm rods in tunic fabric, elbow bends, forearm bracers transitioning to steel gauntlets, and spherical hands with curled finger details.

Adjusting elbow position for a shorter forearm length, then adding blue elbow and shoulder spheres under the pauldron. I'm also sketching out trousers, greaves, and grained leather boots, plus a backpack with a bedroll and small tin cup attached via straps.

For the tabard, I'm skipping any heraldic emblem and instead placing a simple decal plane positioned on the curved torso surface, calculating where it sits flush against the chest without heraldry — just a generic gold-trimmed cloth pattern with a diamond accent.

I'm checking the plane's placement against body curvature so it doesn't visibly float off the surface, adjusting the height range so it sits like a hanging tabard rather than clipping through the strap above it.

Designing the tabard as an SVG texture with a red field, gold border, zigzag trim, and central diamond emblem, sized to scale cleanly onto the box geometry. I'm skipping extra glow effects to keep things simple, and considering using merged geometry for the rivets to stay within part limits.

Writing helper functions...

Now I'm adding details like a cheek piece, a brass butt plate positioned at the stock's end, and a lock plate placed as an ellipsoid offset to the gun's side, plus a hammer rod extending upward from the lock position.

Next I'm working through the barrel's octagonal cross-section, a ramrod placed beneath the barrel with its own offset and wooden material, and the hands -- a fisted sphere with a thumb, tapered forearm leather wrapping, and a steel cuff positioned partway along the forearm.

For the fingers I'll add small knuckle spheres instead of individual digits, keeping it simple. Then I'm positioning the beard as an ellipsoid mass near the chin, checking its scale and offset so it overlaps naturally with the chest without clipping through it.

I'll let the beard overlap the strap naturally rather than avoid it, since a dwarf's beard typically hangs over such straps anyway. I'm positioning the strap diagonally from right shoulder to left hip with a slight embedded midpoint near the beard, then working out the hip ellipsoid endpoint.

Adding cartridge cylinders along the strap, spaced at parameter values that avoid the beard-covered center and concentrated near the shoulder and lower sections, each with brass bodies and dark primer tips.

Now I'm positioning the braids symmetrically on either side, running from near the shoulders down past the belt buckle, using a sequence of spheres with decreasing y, z, and radius values to taper the braid as it hangs, letting it drift slightly away from the body so it floats naturally past the lower beard and torso.

Still working out boot and sole geometry...

Still positioning pauldron details...

Now I'm defining the paint schemes: a steel countershade paint with mottled texture and wear variation for the pauldron, plus a gold paint for trim using similar countershading between lighter and darker tones.

Setting up skin, cloth, and leather colors with mottled countershading and grain textures for added realism, keeping the overall palette small. Defining a Fill type that accepts either a flat color string or a Paint object, then writing a helper function for generating sphere-based parts with configurable position, scale, segments, and optional rotation.

Still writing helpers... adding box and cylinder shape constructors with similar positioning and rotation options, plus a studs function that merges multiple sphere geometries into rivet clusters using mergeGeometries. Now planning out rim rivet placement around the helmet and sketching the lathe outline points for the helmet's curved profile.

Adding horn geometry details...

Positioning the nose guard between the eyes like a helmet nasal, sizing it to clear the nose bulb. Then adding rosy cheek spheres, ear ellipsoids with gold earrings, and starting on the brow shapes.

I notice the helmet brim is overlapping the brows at the current coordinates, so I'm raising the eyes, brows, and helmet base positions and recomputing the head scale and eye placement to fix the collision.

Now I'm positioning the nose, cheeks, mustache, and beard elements, calculating the head surface radius at each y-level to keep the mustache and sideburn ellipsoids flush against the face rather than floating or clipping.

I'm adjusting the helmet's fit over the head, lowering it slightly to close the gap between the helmet rim and the skull surface, then placing the brow ridge, nose guard box, and eye positions relative to the new helmet height, finally tallying up the total figure height including the top of the helmet and horns.

With the horns tipping near 1.4-1.5m, I'm trimming them down a bit since that's tall for a dwarf, bringing the tips to around 1.33-1.36m instead. I'm also placing a ponytail capsule sweeping down behind the head and a backpack box on the back of the torso, then checking whether the ponytail end and the backpack front overlap in z-depth.

Now I'm adding backpack straps as thin rods from the pack to the shoulders, plus a bedroll cylinder lashed across the top of the pack with painted stripes and small buckle details, and a tin cup hanging off the side of the pack.

I'm positioning pouches at the hips - a small box with a flap on one side and a flat canteen shape on the other - checking their placement relative to the arm and torso width so nothing overlaps awkwardly. Then I'll finalize everything and add white highlights to the eyes.

For the gun I'm adding decorative details: gold bands engraved on the barrel, small spherical studs placed along the stock on the visible side using an offset vector perpendicular to the rod axis, and a dark flared muzzle bell at the tip.

Now I'm defining the paint materials: countershaded mottled blue for the torso and sleeves, grain-textured leather in warm browns, and flat dark leather accents, all driven by position and normal functions compatible with the sphere's paint UVs. I'm finalizing and writing out this code carefully to avoid unused variable issues.

Switching to the gun geometry, I'm computing the butt-to-muzzle vector to size the stock, barrel, and flare segments against a realistic blunderbuss length of about 0.76m, then checking hand positions along that vector against elbow joints to confirm arm reach distances are within plausible limits for both the right and left grips.

Checking that the gun doesn't clip into the beard braids or the floor at either end, then planning the left shoulder pauldron placement and simplified hand/finger geometry using small spheres for knuckles and thumb. Now I'm setting up the tabard SVG texture dimensions and defining the box geometry for the front-facing surface.

Writing SVG tabard code...

Fringe bottom can stay transparent, that's fine. Time to finalize and write it out.
